question: Which Plate defaults and public plugin contracts serve a product job, and which duplicate an adequate Plite owner?
method: best-api-review/history-v2; Task complex design; first-principles hard-cut; matched disposable runtime/type prototype
trigger: The user authorized the exact Task investigation named by the preceding Defer review: prototype one descriptor across raw Plite, configured headless Plate and React Plate, then produce the full design and adoption plan.
requirements: Use one public nominal descriptor family and installed portal without moving Plate product authoring into Plite.
Delete synthetic Plate-to-Plite descriptors, global aliases, name-based dependency remapping and late raw-versus-Plate portal dispatch.
Preserve raw Plite independence, immutable author definitions, direct dependency and conflict identity, source ancestry, candidate rollback and retained portal liveness.
Preserve Plate terminal configuration, prior-stage inference, schema-derived behavior, editor-local stores, React exact-view behavior and SSR isolation.
Reject a public compiled-descriptor family, generic compiler registry, opaque metadata replacement or callback casts.
Meet the frozen runtime and TypeScript budgets before accepting the identity target; keep unrelated feature migrations separate, including math, emoji and AI.
evidenceReuse: Rechecked the previous Defer record, current Plite descriptor/registry/portal implementation, Plate descriptor sidecars, author resolver, lowerer, portal adapter and representative raw/headless/React assertions. Built a disposable matched model rather than promoting earlier reference benchmarks. Preserved two failed type-carrier receipts and corrected an initially unfair baseline before using measurements for the verdict.
summary: Pursue one shared plugin descriptor identity and plugin vocabulary while retaining Plate's product compiler. The matched prototype removed synthetic runtime descriptors, aliases, name remaps and portal-kind branches; preserved raw/headless/React lifetimes and rollback; and passed the frozen runtime and TypeScript budgets. The type contract must use a lazy owner-supplied capability provider. Raw Plite author fields remain available while installed behavior moves to a separate record.
alternatives: Keep the current extension/plugin split and adapter: viable fallback, but loses because the prototype demonstrates that the identity, topology and portal translation can disappear without moving product policy.
Rename extension to plugin on the current machinery: reject; it leaves two nominal descriptors and makes the vocabulary lie.
Move Plate stages, configuration, schema, stores and rendering into Plite: reject; raw consumers still do not earn a product compiler.
Make every authored stage carry an eagerly recomputed structural capability accumulator: reject; the matched type run measured 1.65x current instantiations.
Use one Plite nominal reference with a lazy package-owned capability provider and a separate installed record: pursue; it passes the prototype and keeps package ownership honest.
Delete raw descriptor definition fields while splitting installed records: reject absent a separate caller-backed cut; shared identity does not require that extra break.
proofLimits: The disposable model is architectural evidence, not production adoption proof. It ran ten correctness laws, 40 warm samples after eight warmups for 1/32/128/512 descriptors, one descriptive cold observation per cohort, and three interleaved TypeScript 7 diagnostics for 64 raw plus 64 Plate descriptors. Candidate runtime p50 stayed within 1.25x and TypeScript instantiations/memory/check time stayed within their frozen budgets. It did not run current package source, declaration emit, full editor mount/editing latency, browser behavior, packed releases or external consumers. Production implementation must replay those gates and may reverse to the honest split if it fails.
